content: Automated face/plate redaction pipelines commonly fail on: low light, motion blur, faces turned away, plates at sharp angles, small/distant subjects in background. Even 99% recall means 1% of faces ship unredacted -- unacceptable for privacy-critical use since any single miss is a real exposure. Best practice: bias the confidence threshold toward over-blurring (blur everything face-shaped, accept false positives) rather than under-blurring, since a missed detection is worse than an unnecessary blur. Two-stage pipelines (detect -> false-positive removal -> negative-detection handling -> blur) outperform naive one-stage detection which conflates similar-looking objects (e.g., signage as plates).
